title: Wendell Phillips High School and learning tuba from Charlie Allen
summary: Wilson enters Wendell Phillips, joins the ROTC band and is handed a beat-up tuba by Charlie Allen, who teaches him the fingering.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: What high school did you go to?
Wendell Phillips High? A lot of good musicians come out of Wendell Phillips.
Yeah. Did it have a reputation for good musical training then? When was this? About 19 --
Did Wendell Phillips have a reputation as being a good place to study music then?
Yes, we had it then. We had a good musical department. We had an orchestra and we had a band, ROTC band.
Uh-huh. Were you in the ROTC --
That's how I got into the tuba.
Oh, yeah? Tell me about that.
When I started in Phillips High School, a friend of mine belonged to the ROTC band, and I wanted to get in the band. So his name was Charlie Allen.

Mouthpiece maker. So he wanted to know if I -- what instrument I wanted to play. So I couldn't think of nothing else but the bass drums. And he said, 'oh, no.' Said, 'You don't want -- how you going to play bass drum? You can only play bass drum in one band, that's like a military band.'

So I said, 'Well, you got it.' So he went upstairs and come downstairs with an old, beat-up tuba, and handed it to me. So I said, 'What can I do with this, Charlie?' I said, 'this has only got three valves. I play violin with seven positions.' He said, 'That's all right, don't worry about it. I'll teach you.' So he taught me the fingering.
Well, was Charlie a student then, or --
Uh-huh. Who was the band director?
In fact, he was in his senior year, then.
I'm trying to think of it. I can't think of his first name. His last name was Hanson, Captain Hanson.
Captain Hanson. Is that the school that Walter Dyett taught at later?
